content: Certain substances, such as acetaminophen, ascorbic acid, and hydroxyurea, have been demonstrated to interfere with the accuracy of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) readings on specific devices. This interference can result in falsely elevated glucose readings, which may lead to inappropriate clinical decisions if not identified. For individuals utilizing CGM systems, it is essential to regularly review all medications and supplements they are taking, as these substances may impact the reliability of glucose measurements. The American Diabetes Association (ADA) highlights the importance of being aware of substances that can affect CGM accuracy across various device models. It is strongly recommended to cross-check CGM readings with blood glucose monitoring (BGM) to confirm their accuracy and ensure proper diabetes management.
